title: Why You Feel Your Phone Buzz Even When It Has Not
hook: Why do you feel your phone buzz, but it is not really there?

narration.text: Your brain sometimes misinterprets sensory input, leading to phantom phone vibrations.
This is often called phantom vibration syndrome, a type of pareidolia.
Your brain expects a buzz, so it looks for any similar sensation.
Things like clothing rustling or muscle twitches can trigger this false alarm.
Constantly checking your phone trains your brain to be highly alert for its presence.
It is a sign your brain is working hard to keep you connected.
Many people experience this, showing how intertwined we are with our devices.
Do you often feel these phantom vibrations yourself?

description: Ever felt your phone buzz in your pocket, only to find nothing there? This short explains the fascinating psychological reason behind these phantom vibrations. It is all about how our brains interpret everyday sensations.
topic: Why you feel phantom vibrations from your phone when it has not buzzed.
